subject: Post-demo: prompt/output residency and retention — confirmation requested
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: prompt/output residency and retention — confirmation requested

Hi Alex / Nimbus team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the clear priorities. Quick recap and the items we said we'd confirm on:

- Scope: you asked which elements of the inference request/response lifecycle we persist (raw prompts, sanitized prompts, model outputs, debug traces, and KV cache).
- Residency: you want data strictly stored in US regions for this PoC.
- Retention: example TTL ranges and default settings.
- Controls: KMS/HSM support, redaction options, access & audit logs, and proof points (SOC2).

Attached is the questionnaire you sent (Nimbus_security_questionnaire.xlsx). Can you confirm the parts of the questionnaire you need filled first ("PII scope" vs "full telemetry")? That will help us prioritize the answers.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll provide a short written confirmation of default behavior and enterprise-configurable options (by end of day tomorrow).
2) If the PoC requires US-only residency and a DPA, I’ve attached a draft DPA we can start from (DPA_NimbusLabs_draft.docx).
3) If you want to validate audit log retention and KMS keys, we can schedule a 30-min security call with Rishi (our security lead) and your security contact.

High-level summary (short):
- Default (hosted): no persistent prompt/output storage by default for new accounts; ephemeral request logs kept for 72 hours for platform debugging unless customer enables persistent logging.
- Opt-in persistent logging: tenant-configurable, encrypted at rest, tenant-region pinned (US/EU), TTL configurable 0–365 days; can be disabled entirely.
- KV cache / session state: in-memory only; not persisted to disk in hosted mode.

I’ll follow up shortly with Rishi’s formal write-up and the specific answers to your questionnaire items.

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas,

Thanks for the recap — that helps. A couple of clarifying items before the security call so our team can triage:

- When you say "no persistent prompt/output storage by default", can you confirm whether any hashed identifiers, request IDs, or sampling telemetry that could be linked back to content are retained beyond 72 hours? We need to be explicit.
- For opt-in persistent logging: do you offer field-level redaction (PII scrubbing) prior to storage, or is that something Nimbus would need to implement client-side?
- KMS: can we bring our own key (BYOK) in hosted mode, or is BYOK only supported on Dedicated/Private?
- Audit logs: what is contained in those logs (request metadata vs full payloads) and is retention configurable per tenant?

We’ve attached our questionnaire (sheet 2 has the PII fields list) and our security contact asked for an explicit statement on where the data resides for the PoC (US region only) and the maximum retention we can request contractually.

If you can put the answers in writing we’ll circulate internally ahead of the call.

—Alex

Alex / Nimbus security team — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, exportable summary you can include in your risk review. I’ve attached a PDF (security-answers_v1.pdf) with the same content and references to SOC2 artifacts.

Authoritative answers (short):
- Default hosted behavior (new accounts):
  • Prompts and model outputs are NOT persisted to tenant storage by default.
  • Short-lived request traces (service debugging logs) are retained for 72 hours and automatically purged. These traces contain request IDs, timestamps, routing metadata, and anonymized performance metrics but do NOT include persisted full payloads after the 72-hour window.
  • KV cache / session state is in-memory only and is cleared at session termination; not written to persistent disk.

- Opt-in persistent logging (tenant-configurable):
  • If a customer enables persistent logging, request and response payloads are stored encrypted at rest in the tenant’s selected region (US or EU).
  • Retention TTL is configurable per-tenant: 0 (no storage) up to 365 days. Default for paid hosted accounts with no explicit setting is 0 (no persistent storage).
  • Field-level redaction: we offer a server-side redaction pipeline (pattern-based and configurable) that can remove or mask specified PII fields before writes to persistent logs. Customers can also perform client-side redaction prior to sending requests.
  • Sampling: persistent logging supports both full-capture and sampled-capture modes; sampling rate is tenant-configurable.

- BYOK and key management:
  • BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments.
  • For hosted accounts, we offer tenant-key-isolation (separate tenant key envelopes) and integration with KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). BYOK for hosted customers is available on an enterprise add-on and requires a commercial agreement.

- Audit and access logs:
  • Audit logs include user actions (who accessed the console, API key usage events, model deploy/rollback events) and are retained for 90 days for standard customers, and up to 365 days for enterprise customers by contract.
  • Audit logs for forensic requests include metadata only (timestamps, user IDs, request IDs). Full payloads are included in audit extracts only when persistent logging is enabled and when requested per contractual process.

- Residency and contractual commitments:
  • We can pin persistent storage to US regions for your PoC.
  • For customers requiring contractual guarantees (DPA + Annex), we can include a maximum retention ceiling and region clause.

- Encryption, compliance, and controls:
  • All at-rest storage is AES-256 encrypted; keys managed via KMS integrations.
  • In-transit is TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 available).
  • We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts and can provide an audited report under NDA.
  • Role-based access controls, SSO (SAML/SCIM), and least-privilege practices are in place.

- PII redaction and developer tools:
  • Server-side redaction supports regex and field-map policies; redaction is applied before any write to persistent logs.
  • Customers can send redaction directives as part of the API call or define tenant-wide redaction rules via the Console.

- Edge cases and notes:
  • Debugging snapshots (for escalations) can be exported to a secure incident bucket for root-cause analysis; these are timeboxed and require an internal approval workflow.
  • KV cache snapshots do not get persisted in hosted mode. For Dedicated/Private we offer optional snapshot exports controlled by the customer.

Next steps (recommended, actionable):
1) We’ll send the attached security-answers_v1.pdf and a short DPA draft (DPA_NimbusLabs_draft.docx). Please flag any clauses you want expanded (retention ceiling, jurisdiction, BYOK).
2) If you want BYOK for the PoC, let us know and we’ll route to the enterprise onboarding team to scope the add-on.
3) Schedule a 30-min call: proposed times 2028-11-17 09:00 PT or 2028-11-17 13:00 PT. Reply with preferred slot.

If useful, we can also provide a minimal demo showing tenant redaction rules in the Console.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra | Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
